documents.contenu: Last week, a video of a famous actor apologising for a crime he had never committed went viral. Millions of people shared it before experts revealed that it was a deepfake, created with artificial intelligence. "It looked so real," said a student who had shared it. "I didn't even think of checking." The actor's lawyers have announced that they will take legal action. The case has relaunched the debate on how to protect people from fake images.

enonce: "Fiction helps us understand reality." Do you agree? Write about 180 words.
methode: Fais un plan simple : introduction, deux idées, conclusion.
Utilise des connecteurs : *first, moreover, however, therefore, to conclude*.
Réutilise le vocabulaire et la grammaire de l'axe.

corrige.texte: Some people think that fiction is only entertainment. Yet fiction often helps us understand reality.

First, dystopias work as warnings. In *Nineteen Eighty-Four* (1949), George Orwell imagined a society under total surveillance. Today, when we talk about cameras or data collection, we still use the expression "Big Brother".
Moreover, fiction lets us experience other lives. A novel or a film can make us feel what it is like to be someone completely different, which develops empathy.
However, fiction can also be dangerous when it is mistaken for reality, as deepfakes show.
To conclude, I agree with the statement, as long as we remain aware of the difference between the story and the facts.
